data.title: Structural analysis of the intrinsically disordered splicing factor Spp2 and its complex with the DEAH-box ATPase Prp2
data.projectDescription: Structural analysis of spp2 bound to prp2 with chemical crosslinking and mass spectrometry
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: The optimal cross-linker to protein ratio was determined by using 2.5 µg aliquots of the ctPrp2/ctSpp2 complex and a series of cross-linker molar excesses of 5, 10, 25, 50, 100 and 200 as well as a control. Samples were allowed to react with freshly prepared BS3 for 30 minutes at room temperature. The chosen cross-linker to protein ratio was 75, which led to a high yield, yet to a homogeneous sharp band as visualized on SDS-PAGE. The cross-linked samples were analyzed by SDS page on a 4-12% Bis-Tris gel (Invitrogen) with MES as running buffer and stained with Coomassie blue. For MS analysis, both ctPrp2/ctSpp2 was cross-linked with freshly prepared BS3 and EDC (Pierce, Thermo Scientific) in a 75:1 cross-linker to protein ratio, allowed to react and separated as described above. Cross-linked bands were excised from the gel and combined in a single reaction cup according to cross-linking reagent. In gel digestion and extraction of peptides was achieved as described elsewhere (57). The solution of extracted peptides was concentrated on a vacuum evaporator to 5 µL and diluted to a final volume of 10 µl to reach a sample solvent composition of 5% (v/v) CAN, 1% (v/v) FA. Samples were submitted for immediate analysis to the mass spectrometer. Mass spectrometric analysis and cross-link identification were performed as described in detail in the main manuscript.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: Data was processed with Massmatrix according to their publications and manuals. Data search parameters are included in html file results.
